This example report shows the "report" half of Shinylive: **static** prose and figures, plus
**live** Shiny widgets that run entirely in the browser via webR. It hosts on any static web
service because the rendered output is plain files.

Also see the standalone-app half, in `material/apps/penguins-app/`, which is exported with
`shinylive::export()`.

## A static section

This paragraph and the figure below are computed **at render time**: they are baked into the
page as an image. They do not change after publishing.

```{r}
#| label: fig-static
#| fig-cap: "A static figure, computed at build time"
library(ggplot2)
ggplot2::mpg |>
  ggplot(aes(hwy)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "#2E7D6B", color = "white")
```

See @fig-static: it is immutable once rendered. By contrast, the widget that follows is live.

## A live section

The block below is a complete Shiny app, wrapped in a `{shinylive-r}` block. It reacts in the
reader's browser, with no R server involved.

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| markup: code
#| viewerHeight: 460

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  sliderInput("n", "Sample size", min = 10, max = 500, value = 100),
  plotOutput("hist")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$hist <- renderPlot({
    hist(rnorm(input$n), col = "#2E7D6B", main = "Standard normal")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

## A second, data-driven live widget

Here is a widget that works on a small bundled dataset. Because the package list is resolved
from the block, only what the block needs is shipped.

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| layout: vertical
#| viewerHeight: 520

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput("var", "Variable",
              choices = c("bill_length_mm", "bill_depth_mm", "body_mass_g")),
  plotOutput("hist")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  penguins <- palmerpenguins::penguins  # small, always available demo data
  output$hist <- renderPlot({
    hist(penguins[[input$var]], col = "#4A5899", main = input$var)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

## Sharing

Render this file, then publish the HTML anywhere static:

```
quarto publish gh-pages
quarto publish netlify
quarto publish quarto-pub
```

Or zip the folder and send it: a collaborator unzips and opens the HTML to run the widgets
locally, fully offline.
